# Indicators

The small labels that say how something is: its state, how many, how much it moved; the words carry the meaning.

**Kind:** Pattern

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/Indicators/Indicators.mdx`

## The three tags

Three jobs, three components. A category with a color is a Tag, not an indicator.

## Key cases

- **Status in a row.** Default spacing in a table cell. One status per object; the label is one or two words.
- **Status beside a heading.** Spacious beside the page title, after the text.
- **Counts on navigation.** A count beside an item's name. At zero the component renders nothing; bold asks for action now, at most one per area.
- **Where color is not enough.** A leading icon joins the color on a status that must be told apart at a glance, such as Missed.
- **Change where up is bad.** Absences rose by 3: the value is up and the tone is danger, because the good direction is down.
- **A roll-up.** A group's status shows the worst state among its children: danger over warning over information.

A checklist tracks setup or compliance steps in three layouts: a dismissible card on Home, a persistent card in a page, and a compact summary at the foot of the Sidebar.

## Usage

Use Indicators when something needs a small label that says how it is. Ask what the label says: a number is a Count tag; a condition that can change is a Status tag; how much a number moved is a Change tag; a subject, a person or a category is a Tag. Skip an indicator when no action follows from it; past five or six states, use text.

| The label says | Component | Looks | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The condition something is in, and it can change | Status tag | Fill by meaning: neutral not started, information in progress, success done, warning needs attention, danger failed or missed, discovery new | "Needs review" |
| How many | Count tag | Subtle neutral; bold for action now; nothing at 0; a cap past `max` with "+" | "12", "99+" |
| How much it moved | Change tag | Signed value, arrow, tone from the good direction; neutral when there is no judgment | "+3 vs last week" |
| A category, a subject, a person | Tag | Outline and text; a leading visual is optional | "Lincoln Middle" |
| Setup or compliance steps left to finish | Checklist (`Card` + `Section` + `Progress bar`) | Header count and bar aligned to one 128 action column; open steps above done steps | "2 of 5 done" |
| The shape of a trend | Sparkline (Planned) | A word-sized line beside the number | Attendance over eight weeks |

## Alternatives

- For a message about the thing, use a Section message or a Flag; the Notifications pattern picks between them.
- For a due or event date, use `DateTag`.
- For a competency, use `SmartTag`.
- For something the AI proposes, use `Suggestion`.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Status in one or two words: "Scheduled", "Needs review", "Missed". | "This session has been missed". |
| Count as the bare number: "4", "12", "99+". | "4 items", "Count: 4". |
| Change signed, with the comparison: "+3 vs last week", "−12%". | "3 more", "went up". |
| Hidden text reads the whole thing: "Up 3 vs last week". | Nothing for the screen reader. |

## Accessibility

- A tag is read as its text; nothing suggests it can be pressed. A clipped tag becomes a tab stop so the Tooltip opens on focus.
- A count's meaning is in the label it sits on: "Inbox, 3 unread". A bare number announces nothing useful.
- A Change tag's arrow and value are hidden from assistive technology and its words read the direction and the comparison.
- A Status tag, Tag and Change tag keep an inside border, so a pale fill stays visible on any background and in forced colors.

## Parts

| Part | Component | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| State | Status tag | Six appearances; `trailingMetric` nests a count inside it. |
| How many | Count tag | `max` caps it, `isBold` asks for action, `label` names it for a screen reader. |
| How much it moved | Change tag | `goodDirection` sets the tone; `comparison` names what it is measured against. |
| Checklist | Card, Section, Progress bar | Composed step rows (`Icon`, text, `Button` or "Completed" text) on `--checklist-action-width`; `Icon button` dismisses an optional card. |
| Category | Tag | Not an indicator: a subject, a person or a category. |

## Related

- Notifications: use for the count on the bell and the Inbox.
- Overflow: use for a tag that clips.
- Navigation: use for counts on Sidebar items and tabs.

## Motion

Indicators reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| status | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-default` | A status that changes fades to its new word and fill on appearance.default; nothing bounces. |
| count-first | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | A count rolls once on first view, downward, and then fades to later values on appearance.fast. |
| progress | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-linear` | Progress fills on linear with the work, never ahead. Nothing bounces. |

## Best practices

### Never let color carry the meaning alone. {#never-let-color-carry-the-meaning-alone}

**Checked:** Review

The words say the state; the fill repeats it. A state that must be told apart at a glance adds a leading icon. A Change tag's arrow is decorative and its hidden text reads "Up 3 vs last week". A dot with no label is announced as nothing.

### Give each appearance one meaning. {#give-each-appearance-one-meaning}

**Checked:** Review

Neutral is not started, info is in progress, success is done, warning needs attention, danger failed or missed, discovery is new. Success never labels a problem. There is no color prop; a category with a color is a Tag.

Do: Danger on a missed session: the word and the fill agree.
Don't: Success on a missed session: the fill says good about bad news.

### Show one status per object. {#show-one-status-per-object}

**Checked:** Review

Two statuses force people to decide which is true. A roll-up shows the worst child state.

### Keep a status to one or two words. {#keep-a-status-to-one-or-two-words}

**Checked:** Review

A status is read at a glance; a sentence belongs in the row text. A Status tag truncates at 200 with its full text in a Tooltip.

### Keep most counts quiet and show nothing at zero. {#keep-most-counts-quiet-and-show-nothing-at-zero}

**Checked:** Automatic

Subtle neutral is the default. Bold asks for action now, so at most one bold count per area. Pass the raw number: the component renders nothing at 0 and caps past `max` with a "+". No skeleton on a count; it appears when the number arrives.

### Set the Change tag's good direction so up can be bad. {#set-the-change-tag-s-good-direction-so-up-can-be-bad}

**Checked:** Automatic

The sign gives the direction; the good direction gives the tone: up, down or none. Absences rising is danger; sessions held rising is success; a change with no judgment stays neutral. The value is always signed.

Do: A rise in absences in danger: the good direction is down.
Don't: A rise in absences in success: the color says good about bad news.

### Edit a status in the field, not on the label. {#edit-a-status-in-the-field-not-on-the-label}

**Checked:** Review

A Status tag never opens a menu. Where a status can be changed, the field around it becomes an inline Select.

### Nest a count in a status instead of placing one beside it. {#nest-a-count-in-a-status-instead-of-placing-one-beside-it}

**Checked:** Review

"Needs review 3" reads as one label; two labels side by side read as unrelated.

### Line up checklist actions in one column and mark done steps with text. {#line-up-checklist-actions-in-one-column-and-mark-done-steps-with-text}

**Checked:** Review

Build the checklist from `PatternCard` and `PatternSection`:

1. Compose each row from an `Icon`, step text with one fact, and an action column. Use `--checklist-action-width` (128), with `--checklist-action-min-width` (120) as its floor. Buttons fill the column and align down the list.
2. Put the title at the header's start and the count ("2 of 5 done") with a `ProgressBar` at the end. Align the bar's start edge with the action column: 128 wide on a persistent card, or 96 when a 32 dismiss `IconButton` occupies the end.
3. Keep open steps in order above completed steps. Center a check icon and plain "Completed" text (Body small, subtle) in each completed row's action column.

Choose the layout by where the checklist appears:

| Layout | Use | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dismissible card | Home | When complete, shrinks to one line for a day, then disappears. |
| Persistent card | Required work on a page | Keeps every completed row visible. |
| Compact card | Foot of the Sidebar | Shows the count, progress bar and next step, which opens the full list. |
